listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Wednesday, November 4. Our lead story is the election. Democrats have won full control of Congress, according to NPR News. The wins in the House and Senate return the party to control of both chambers for the first time since 2023. NPR says this deepens the expected friction with President Trump, and calls it a new era of divided government. Now the front page. Anthropic has filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the Securities and Exchange Commission. It relates to a proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock. In Georgia, former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms defeated Republican Rick Jackson. She is the first Democrat elected Georgia governor in more than twenty years. And Iran's chief negotiator said Americans voted no to war. Donald Trump acknowledged the conflict's role in the Republican Party's defeat. Now the sections. In tech, Simon Willison tests a Qwen model on his laptop against a new paper on language models reading and writing neural network weights. Worktrunk, a tool for managing Git worktrees for parallel AI agent workflows, is trending on GitHub. Anthropic also announced an expanded partnership with GSA to bring Claude to all levels of government. In politics, Democrats flipped the Texas Senate seat with James Talarico, and Gina Hinojosa ousted Governor Greg Abbott. In South Carolina, Annie Andrews defeated Senator Darline Graham. The Lever begins a series asking whether Democrats will deliver the change it says voters wanted. In world news, the death toll from the Russian strike on a Ukrainian aid site reached twenty nine, with forty eight still missing. India's navy rescued twenty crew from an Iranian fishing boat hijacked off Somalia. In sports, DeForest Buckner says it is Super Bowl or bust after returning to the 49ers by trade. Houston, seven and one, hosts Minnesota. And Tom Nolan knocked out Renato Moicano at UFC Vegas 123. In Atlanta, Democrats gained control of the Georgia Public Service Commission for the first time in decades. Senator Jon Ossoff won a second term. A civil rights landmark on the Westside has reopened as housing. In architecture, Autom8Labs launched skills that guide AI agents through tasks in Revit and other tools. nCircle Tech launched an AI app builder called nVibe. ArchDaily looks at the Drill Hall in Johannesburg. In science, a study found microplastics in nearly two thirds of corals in a Malaysian marine protected area. NASA shared a photo from the October twenty ninth spacewalk. And hawkmoths have evolved three ways to jam bat sonar. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Democrats win full control of Congress, ushering in a new era of divided government
lead.note: Democrats have won full control of Congress, according to NPR News. The victories in the House and Senate return the party to control of both chambers for the first time since 2023. The report says the result deepens the level of expected friction between Congress and President Trump, and it describes the outcome as a new era of divided government. For a reader following domestic politics, this matters because a Democratic Congress will now face President Trump directly. Many of today's other stories, from Georgia to Texas to South Carolina, are results from the same election night. The politics and Atlanta sections carry those state and local outcomes, and the front page has the Georgia governor's race. The summary gives no seat counts, so the exact margins are still to be confirmed elsewhere.
